nodes.title: The docsmirror CLI
nodes.summary: Four commands: check, the anti-rot gate; manifest, which generates the documentation map; serve, the local reading and editing app; and export, a static, read-only copy of it.

anchors.title: The docsmirror CLI
anchors.summary: Four commands: check, the anti-rot gate; manifest, which generates the documentation map; serve, the local reading and editing app; and export, a static, read-only copy of it.

anchors.title: docsmirror check
anchors.summary: It reads every source file of a project, finds the @docs pointers, and fails when one no longer resolves.

anchors.title: Options
anchors.summary: docsmirror check [projectRoot] accepts an explicit project root; it defaults to the current working directory.

anchors.title: What check verifies
anchors.summary: Exit codes: 0 when nothing is reported, 1 when anything is, 2 on a usage error, an unknown flag, an unreadable configuration file, a docs root that does not exist.

anchors.title: Configuration

anchors.title: Include and exclude

anchors.title: Generating the manifest
anchors.summary: The manifest describes the whole documentation surface for machines to read; what it contains and why it is generated rather than written is in The manifest.

anchors.title: Orphan detection
anchors.summary: Off by default, enabled with --orphans.

anchors.title: docsmirror serve
anchors.summary: Binding beyond loopback is an explicit opt-in with real consequences: the app writes to the files in your working tree, so anyone who can reach the port can edit your documentation.

anchors.title: docsmirror export
anchors.summary: Writes a static, read-only copy of the web app to a folder: the same front end, reading from JSON baked in at export time instead of a live server, ready to host anywhere that serves plain files,…

anchors.title: The MCP server
anchors.summary: The manifest is what an agent needs; MCP is how it actually gets it.

anchors.title: Why an agent needs this
anchors.summary: Without a map, an agent looking for a decision has two bad options: read the whole docs folder, or guess a filename.

anchors.title: Tools
anchors.summary: search_documentation is honest lexical search: a hit in a title or an anchor outranks a hit in the body, and a whole word outranks a substring.

anchors.title: Resources
anchors.summary: Every document is also exposed as an MCP resource at docs://<path>, with the document's title as its name and its derived summary as its description.

anchors.title: Freshness
anchors.summary: The server builds the manifest from the live filesystem on the first tool call, it does not require a committed docsmirror.json, and rebuilds it when a documentation file changes on disk.

anchors.title: What it deliberately does not do
anchors.summary: It does not write.

anchors.title: The pointers request

anchors.title: The section request

anchors.title: Diagnostics

anchors.title: Definition
anchors.summary: Go-to-definition on a pointer jumps to the markdown file, positioned at the heading line of the anchored section, or at the top of the document for a bare pointer.

anchors.title: Document links
anchors.summary: The pointer range is also published as a document link with the same target, so ctrl-click works in clients that prefer links to definitions.

anchors.title: Pointer index
anchors.summary: Hover, inlay hints, definition, links and diagnostics all ask the same question of the same text.
